Implemented the PATCH contract.

## Changes

**`src/parser.ts`** — rewrote `parseProfile` to the full contract:
- Rejects non-objects, `null`, arrays, and objects whose prototype is neither `Object.prototype` nor `null`.
- Rejects any own key other than `displayName`/`tags` (checked via `Reflect.ownKeys`, so non-enumerable and symbol keys count too).
- `displayName`: absent → `keep`; `null` → set to `null`; string → trimmed, must be 1–40 chars after trimming; any other type (numbers, booleans, `undefined`, boxed strings, arrays) → invalid without coercion.
- `tags`: absent → `keep`; `null` or `[]` → set to a fresh empty array; otherwise must be an array of ≤5 elements, each a string, trimmed to 1–12 chars, with uniqueness enforced after trimming; non-string elements are invalid (no filtering/coercion). The stored array is always newly built, so the caller's array is never reused.
- All failures throw exactly `Error('invalid profile')`; a top-level guard converts any hostile input (throwing getters/proxies) to that same error. Parsing is fully completed before the service mutates anything, so invalid patches leave storage untouched.

**`src/service.ts`** — `ProfileService.patch` parses first, then applies only `set` fields to the stored profile and returns it; an empty object performs no assignments (safe no-op).

**`checks/contract.cjs`** — added a comprehensive check covering bounds, trimming, dedupe, null/empty clears, unknown keys, prototypes, null-prototype inputs, non-mutation of input, no tag-array aliasing, and unchanged storage on every failure mode.

Public interfaces (`ProfileService`, `patch`, `parseProfile`, `types.ts`) are unchanged.

## Verification

```
tsc -p tsconfig.json && node checks/public.cjs   # passes
node checks/contract.cjs                          # "contract checks passed"
```

Also validated adversarial cases: frozen stored profiles with an empty patch, throwing getters/proxies, sparse tag arrays, and non-enumerable extra keys.
